phase_assessment.claim: The exact eight-item affirmative presentation was admitted with one spoken frontier label per frozen script reference, followed by a successful interface-understanding check.
All eight original affirmative base items were admitted and scored 7/8. Cup, plate, spoon, bowl, knife, glass, and napkin were correct; fork was selected as knife.

The fork error at sequence 29 was not followed immediately by its required PRESENT_AGAIN dispatch, replay, and cold retest. The block advanced through items six, seven, and eight before a delayed dispatch was attempted.

The harness rejected the delayed PRESENT_AGAIN event because it attempted to move backward from the already-admitted item-eight position to item five, then froze the run at sequence 36. No PRESENT_AGAIN tool call, replay exposure, or cold-retest response was admitted.
Negative, W-question, OR-question, mixed-practice, picture-book, comprehension, transfer, and closing-recap phases were not reached and therefore were not demonstrated.

learner_capability_hypotheses.claim: The only complete response set is the narrow affirmative base selection block, which scored 7/8 after immediate presentation. This does not establish the complete controlled square, mixed retrieval, transfer, story comprehension, or retention.
Recovery or persistence for the fork-to-knife error is not demonstrated because its replay and cold retest were never admitted.
Capability on every later required phase is not demonstrated because the run froze before those phases began.

remaining_difficulties.claim: The learner's response to a valid fork re-presentation and fresh unscored retest remains unknown.
The complete controlled square, mixed practice, story comprehension, unseen transfer, closing recap, and delayed retention remain untested.
No learner difficulty can explain the terminal alarm: the alarm arose from a backward orchestration attempt after the broker had already advanced beyond the failed item.

uncertainties: The run is too incomplete to infer lesson-level acquisition from one immediately presented selection block.
The missing fork cold retest prevents any distinction between a transient selection error, a visual fork/knife confusion, and a persistent label problem.

The broker/operator workflow linted the delayed dispatch unsuccessfully but nevertheless continued to the append boundary; the report cannot infer what a correctly stopped preflight would have produced because no corrected intervention was admitted.

The log attributes the rejected proposed tool event syntactically to the teacher actor, but the evidence context identifies a broker/operator scheduling and append-control failure. It should not be reclassified as a learner, lesson-plan, or conductor-routine failure.
The lesson's later dosage, story, comprehension, transfer, recap, and finish behavior cannot be evaluated from this alarm-frozen prefix.
No rehearsal observation can advance actual learner state.

intervention_assessment.claim: PRESENT_AGAIN was warranted immediately after the incorrect fork response at sequence 29, but no intervention event was admitted at that decision boundary.

The later PRESENT_AGAIN proposal at sequence 36 carried the mapped fork dispatch, but it was no longer admissible after events 30 through 35 advanced the frozen execution position through knife, glass, and napkin.
The harness correctly rejected the backward dispatch and sounded ALARM. No malformed tool event, replay, or cold-retest pair was admitted after the final valid learner response.
TRAIN_MORE, TRAIN_LONGER, REPLAY_LESSON, and FINISH were not reached and cannot be judged from this run.

teacher_self_critique: The admitted presentation and affirmative teacher turns were exact, locally ordered, and language-licensed. The conductor routine itself did not generate the terminal sequencing failure.

The fork error at sequence 29 created an immediate adaptive decision boundary. The broker should have stopped admission there, dispatched and linted PRESENT_AGAIN, replayed the exact fork presentation turn, and appended the mapped cold retest before allowing item six.

Once items six through eight had been admitted, attempting the item-five dispatch necessarily moved backward across frozen execution order. The broker/operator append controller, not learner capability or lesson content, caused that terminal conflict.

A failed lint must be terminal for that append attempt. Continuing to append after lint failure defeated the purpose of preflight and converted a locally detectable orchestration mistake into an alarm-frozen run.

The broker should maintain a pending-intervention lock keyed to the failed base item. While that lock is open, it must reject later base-item artifacts until dispatch, exact replay, and cold retest have all passed lint and been admitted.
Because only one controlled family was observed, I must not generalize the 7/8 affirmative result into broad lexical capability or claim that the lesson, visual material, or teaching routine failed.
alarm_assessment: The harness ALARM at sequence 36 was warranted and correctly terminal. The last valid execution position was affirmative item eight at sequences 34-35; the proposed PRESENT_AGAIN then targeted failed item five and therefore attempted a backward move across frozen order. Primary root cause is infrastructure/orchestration: the broker failed to stop at the item-five adaptive boundary, allowed items six through eight to be admitted, then continued toward append after dispatch lint had failed. This is not evidence of learner failure, lesson-plan failure, visual-material failure, or Luna-routine failure. The harness preserved integrity by rejecting the proposed tool event and freezing the run.
